title: New IT Rules - obligations social media platforms still ignore
p1:
Millions of people use social media every day, but many don't know that platforms have legal responsibilities beyond simply hosting content.

The surprising part? Some of these obligations are still ignored or poorly followed, even after the introduction of New IT Rules.
p2:
Many users think social media companies are only like digital notice boards. They are not. Under the rules, platforms must take steps like responding to user complaints, appointing grievance officers, and following specific procedures for handling harmful content.

One thing many people don't know: large platforms may have additional compliance duties because of their size and impact on public conversations.
p3:
These rules are not about removing every opinion people disagree with. They are meant to create accountability when illegal content, privacy concerns, or user complaints arise.

For users and businesses, the practical takeaway is simple: knowing your rights online helps you question platforms when they fail to follow their own responsibilities.
conclusion: Do you think social media platforms are doing enough to follow their legal obligations, or should there be stricter accountability?
